questions.question: How tall is the Millau Viaduct in southern France at its highest point, in metres?
questions.note: It culminates at 343 metres — higher than the Eiffel Tower — and its 2,460-metre deck touches the Tarn valley in only nine places.

questions.question: Which tennis Grand Slam is older: Wimbledon or Roland-Garros?
questions.note: Wimbledon, the oldest of the four majors, was founded in 1877; the French championship followed in 1891.

questions.question: Put these four battles of the Hundred Years' War in chronological order, earliest first.
questions.note: England won the first three, but Castillon in July 1453 was the French victory that ended the war and left England holding only Calais.

questions.question: Four French cheeses. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: Camembert, Livarot and Pont-l'Évêque are Normandy PDO cheeses, each named after a Normandy village. Reblochon comes from Savoie, in the Alps.

questions.question: Put these four Paris landmarks in order of when they were built, earliest first.
questions.answer: Notre-Dame, Eiffel Tower, Centre Pompidou, Louvre Pyramid
questions.note: Notre-Dame took nearly a century to build; the Eiffel Tower went up in about two years for the 1889 Exposition Universelle.

questions.question: What was Concorde's maximum cruising speed, in kilometres per hour?
questions.note: That's Mach 2.04, more than twice the speed of sound, which cut London–New York to about three hours.

questions.question: Four islands. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: Jersey, Alderney and Sark are all Channel Islands off the French coast. The Isle of Man is also a Crown Dependency, but it sits in the Irish Sea.

questions.question: Put these four events of the French Revolution in chronological order, earliest first.
items: Declaration of the Rights of Man (26 August 1789)
questions.answer: Storming of the Bastille, Declaration of the Rights of Man, Execution of Louis XVI, Coup of 18 Brumaire
questions.note: The whole revolutionary decade runs from the fall of the Bastille to Bonaparte's coup, barely ten years apart.

questions.question: Which national stadium holds more people: Wembley or the Stade de France?
questions.note: Wembley seats 90,000, the largest in the UK, against roughly 80,000 at the Stade de France.

questions.question: How many official Eon Productions James Bond films did Sean Connery star in as 007?
questions.note: Dr. No, From Russia with Love, Goldfinger, Thunderball, You Only Live Twice and Diamonds Are Forever — the later Never Say Never Again wasn't an Eon film.

questions.question: Four French spirits. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: Cognac and Armagnac are distilled from wine and marc from the pressed skins and pips — all three start with grapes. Calvados is distilled from cider.

questions.question: Which opened first: the London Underground or the Paris Métro?
questions.note: London's Metropolitan Railway carried its first passengers in January 1863, some 37 years before the Paris Métro opened in 1900.

questions.question: How long is the River Thames, from its source in the Cotswolds to the North Sea, in kilometres?
questions.note: At 346 km (215 miles) the Thames is the longest river entirely in England, though the Severn is longer overall.

questions.question: The Hundred Years' War ran from 1337 to 1453 — so how many years did it actually last?
questions.note: 'The Hundred Years' War' is rather catchier than 'the 116 Years' War'.

questions.question: Which horse race is older: the Epsom Derby or the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe?
questions.note: The Derby was first run at Epsom Downs in 1780, a full 140 years before the Arc was inaugurated at Longchamp in 1920.

questions.question: The dish 'chicken Marengo' is named after a battle won by which commander?
questions.note: It celebrates Napoleon's victory over the Austrians at Marengo, in northern Italy, in June 1800.

questions.question: Put these four Beatles albums in order of release, earliest first.
items: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band (1967)
questions.answer: Please Please Me, Rubber Soul, Sgt. Pepper's, Abbey Road
questions.note: The Beatles went from their debut to Abbey Road in only six and a half years.

questions.question: In what year did France's first TGV service, between Paris and Lyon, start carrying passengers?
questions.note: The first commercial services on the new LGV Sud-Est ran on 27 September 1981, launching high-speed rail in France.

questions.question: Four French place names. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: Brittany, Normandy and Occitanie are all administrative régions. The Dordogne is a département, inside the région of Nouvelle-Aquitaine.

questions.question: The suits on a British pack of cards — spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs — were adopted from which country's cards?
questions.note: English decks took their suits from French cards standardised by the mid-15th century; the Germans settled on acorns, leaves, hearts and bells.

questions.question: Put these four monarchs in order of when they came to the throne, earliest first.
questions.answer: William the Conqueror, Henry VIII, Queen Anne, Queen Victoria
questions.note: Anne was the first monarch of the united Kingdom of Great Britain, reigning from 1702 to 1714.

questions.question: Which came first: the very first Cannes Film Festival, or the very first BAFTA film awards?
questions.note: Cannes opened its first festival in September 1946; the first British Film Academy Awards were handed out in May 1949.

questions.question: Which French chef, who ran the kitchens of London's Savoy Hotel, wrote the 1903 cookery classic 'Le Guide Culinaire'?
questions.note: Escoffier developed its 5,000-odd recipes while cooking at the Savoy, Ritz and Carlton hotels in London.

questions.question: Which everyday medical instrument did the French doctor René Laennec invent in 1816?
questions.note: Laennec first rolled up sheets of paper into a tube to listen to a patient's chest; the wooden cylinder he then made became the stethoscope.

questions.question: Four protected landscapes in southern England. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: Dartmoor, Exmoor and the New Forest are National Parks. The Cotswolds is a National Landscape — what used to be called an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

questions.question: Put these four moments of the Napoleonic era in chronological order, earliest first.
questions.note: Austerlitz fell exactly one year after the coronation, and just six weeks after Nelson had destroyed the Franco-Spanish fleet at Trafalgar.

questions.question: Which city hosted the modern Olympic Games first: Paris or London?
questions.note: Paris staged the Games in 1900, eight years before London's first turn in 1908 — which is still the longest Olympics ever, running six months.

questions.question: Which French director made his feature debut in 1959 with 'The 400 Blows', a cornerstone of the Nouvelle Vague?
questions.note: Truffaut's semi-autobiographical first feature introduced Antoine Doinel and won him the Best Director prize at Cannes.

questions.question: Three of these belong in the protected recipe for a Cornish pasty. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: Under its PGI, a real Cornish pasty is made in Cornwall from beef, potato, onion and swede — carrot has no place in it.

questions.question: In what year did Stephenson's Rocket win the Rainhill Trials?
questions.note: Rocket was the only engine to finish the nine days of trials near Liverpool in October 1829, hitting 30 mph and taking the £500 prize.
